# Wenchuan-Zhang/CaseScope
**Stars**: 1 | **Language**: Python
**Description**: This repository contains the evaluation code for the CaseScope pathology benchmark. CaseScope is designed to evaluate multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on diagnosing pathology cases using a series of H&E fields ordered by magnification. It includes a large dataset of 1,236 cases, 4,941 fields, and 843 diagnostic entities across 18 organ systems, with tasks focusing on open-ended diagnosis, multiple-choice diagnosis, behavior triage, ordinal grading, finding verification, and finding location.

CaseScope: A Multi-Field Benchmark for Case-Level Pathology Diagnosis with Multimodal LLMs

# ✨ News + [Nov 2026] 📄 The paper is on [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.15325). + [Nov 2026] 🚀 **CaseScope released**: the benchmark data on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/WenchuanZhang/CaseScope) and the evaluation code in this repository. ## 📖 Overview

Pathologists rarely diagnose from a single image: they scan a section at low power for architecture, zoom into selected fields for cytology, and integrate the evidence across views and scales. CaseScope evaluates multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on exactly this setting: **diagnosis of a case from several curated H&E fields of one lesion** (for atlas figure series, of one disease), ordered from low to high magnification. It consists of **1,236 cases** with **4,941 fields**, covering **843 diagnostic entities** across **18 organ systems**, and poses **4,679 items** in **six tasks**: * 🏥 **CaseScope-Teaching**: 436 cases from an in-house image library for pathology residency training, 2 to 8 fields per case (median 5), 390 entities including non-neoplastic, benign and rare ones * 📚 **CaseScope-Atlas**: 800 cases from 88 published pathology atlases, one case per entity, 453 entities without a Teaching case ## 🧪 Tasks | Task | Description | Teaching | Atlas | Metric | |---|---|---:|---:|---| | **A1** | Open-ended diagnosis (JSON: diagnosis, two differentials, confidence) | 436 | 800 | HDS, exact, top-3 | | **A2** | Diagnosis, 10-way multiple choice; distractors from the ontology include each entity's classic look-alikes | 436 | 800 | CircularEval (10 rotations) | | **B** | Behaviour triage: non-neoplastic, benign, intermediate, malignant | 380 | 762 | CircularEval, critical miss rate | | **C** | Ordinal grading (e.g. DCIS nuclear grade, Gleason pattern, endometrial dating) | 44 | - | CircularEval, quadratic weighted kappa | | **R1** | Finding verification: four true/false statements on low-power architecture or high-power cytology | 390 | 195 | statement and item accuracy | | **G1** | Finding location: which field shows a described finding | - | 436 | CircularEval over the option rotations | ## Benchmark Construction ### CaseScope-Teaching The library was built by selecting common diseases from pathology textbooks, scanning the corresponding slides, and having four pathologists independently collect fields at several magnifications and jointly select the representative ones. Because the library files the same case under several organ systems and names, we treat construction as a reconstruction problem: - **Duplicates and cases**: every copy of a picture (exact, re-encoded, resized or colour-edited) is found by file and perceptual hashes and pathology-CLIP similarity confirmed at the pixel level; copies of a case are merged - **De-identification**: all EXIF, ICC and XMP metadata removed, opaque identifiers - **Ontology**: labels harmonised to 407 entities aligned with the WHO Classification of Tumours (5th edition), with a behaviour class and an H&E-sufficiency prior per entity - **Field order**: ranked by a zero-shot magnification score and checked case by case by a pathologist - **Quality control**: an automated pre-review flagged doubtful cases and items, each re-examined by a pathologist ### CaseScope-Atlas Panels that share a caption form a case of one lesion, and consecutive figures of one entity a case of one disease. Each case is mapped from its caption to the ontology (extended by 439 entities) by two LLMs that must agree, and the labels were verified by a pathologist. Taking one case per entity, common diagnoses first, gives 800 cases. ## Evaluation Framework ### 🎯 Protocol - **Prompt**: one user turn and no system prompt; the fields, each preceded by its number (`Image i:`), then the question, the options and the answer instruction - **Decoding**: greedy, up to 1,024 new tokens (4,096 for reasoning models). A reasoning model still reasoning at the limit is given the stop-thinking instruction and answers from there - **Parsing**: a deterministic parser reads the committed answer; responses it cannot map go to an LLM judge, and unmapped answers count as wrong ### 🔄 CircularEval Every multiple-choice item is asked once per rotation of its options (A2: 10, B: 4, C: 2 to 4, G1: one per field) and counts as correct only if every rotation is answered correctly, which exposes answer-position bias and unstable choices. ### 🩺 Hierarchical Diagnostic Score (A1) 1 for the reference entity, a synonym or an accepted alternate; 0.5 for another entity of the same family and behaviour; 0 otherwise. The item score is the higher of an LLM judge's grade (Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct-AWQ) and a deterministic ontology match. ### 🔬 Field-set Ablations `single_best` (only the highest-power field), `nosite` (no specimen site) and `noimage` (the question without its fields) test whether a model uses the fields at all. ## 📊 Evaluation Results Main results of the paper (%; A2, B, C, G1: CircularEval; A1: HDS;
